scenes.text: At the double doors of the vascular gallery, imagine four number locks above the frame. Widening the doorway changes resistance through a fourth-power relationship.
scenes.spokenText: At the double doors of the vascular gallery, imagine four number locks above the frame. Widening the doorway changes resistance through a fourth-power relationship.

scenes.text: For steady laminar flow in the ideal tube model, resistance is proportional to viscosity and length, and inversely proportional to the fourth power of radius.
scenes.spokenText: For steady laminar flow in the ideal tube model, resistance is proportional to viscosity and length, and inversely proportional to the fourth power of radius.

scenes.text: If diameter doubles, radius doubles too. Raise that factor of two to the fourth power: two times two times two times two equals sixteen.
scenes.spokenText: If diameter doubles, radius doubles too. Raise that factor of two to the fourth power: two times two times two times two equals sixteen.

scenes.text: Resistance therefore becomes one sixteenth of its original value when length and viscosity stay unchanged. Starting from sixteen resistance units, the new value is one unit.
scenes.spokenText: Resistance therefore becomes one sixteenth of its original value when length and viscosity stay unchanged. Starting from sixteen resistance units, the new value is one unit.

scenes.text: This is an idealized laminar-flow relationship. In real circulation, pulsation, branching, and vessel compliance affect how pressure and flow behave. Keep the model assumptions in mind.
scenes.spokenText: This is an idealized laminar-flow relationship. In real circulation, pulsation, branching, and vessel compliance affect how pressure and flow behave. Keep the model assumptions in mind.

scenes.text: Return to the double doors and the four locks. Remember: double diameter, divide resistance by sixteen. The answer to this example is one peripheral resistance unit.
